newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine 5-mth exports rise 22.7 to $9.558 bln.
newsitem.headline: Philippine 5-mth exports rise 22.7 to $9.558 bln.

text.p: Earnings of Philippine exports grew by 22.7 percent in the first five months of the year to $9.558 billion, the National Statistics Office said on Friday.
Exports in the first five months of 1996 stood at $7.789 billion.
Export receipts for the month of May alone stood at $1.970 billion, up 22.2 percent from $1.612 billion in the year-ago period.

Overseas sales were led by electronics and components which surged 32.4 percent to $881.8 million in May from the year-earlier $665.9 million. Electronics accounted for 44.8 percent of May exports, the agency said.

Garments, which was the second biggest earner with a 9.6 percent share, was almost unchanged at $189.9 million in May from $189.8 million last year. Since last year, garments had been outpriced by other countries in the world market.
The U.S. was the destination of most of the country's exports with a 34.1 percent share, or $672.4 million, of the total in May.

The other leading export markets were Japan, with a 16.7 percent share or $328.5 million; Netherlands, 6.2 percent or $121.5 million; Singapore, 5.8 percent or $114.2 million; Hong Kong, five percent or $99 million.
